intention for november - for the proper use of wealth let us pray for the proper use of wealth, that not succumbing to the tempt ation of selfishness, it may always be put at the service for the common good and solidarity of those who have less. ‘against this backdrop, there has been “troubling revival of war as an instrument of international politics ” (ibid.,190). as the catechism of the catholic church states, “the accumulation of arms strikes many as a paradoxically suitable way of deterring potential adversaries from war. they see it as the most effective means of ensuring peace among nations ” (no. 2315), thus betraying the memory of the twentieth century and the senseless slaughter of millions of human lives. precisely in these times marked by a “culture of power, ” there is a need to cultivate the spirit of assisi, which entails a rejection of the religious justification of war, a spirit of mediation and dialogue, and contemplative reflection combined with creative action in the service of a fu ture of peace. yes, peace must once again become the common ideal of all peoples, the gu iding star for all our choices, the standard that exposes injustice, and the shared horizon for a ll. we must rebuild peace everywhere, not prepare for more wars. war can never be waged in the name of god. for us believers, “to fight in the name of religion means attacking religion itself ” 2self (magnifica humanitas, 223). there is no such thing as a holy war: only peace is holy. that is why the journey begun in assisi as a shared quest for peace is, first and fore most, the path of prayer. prayer may seem weak in the face of the powers of the world, but it is the humble strength of believers. let us turn to god, the giver of peace, that he may touch the hearts of those who seek war and terrorism. let us not forget that prayer is never in vain. ’ message of his holiness pope leoxiv to the participants in the international meeting ‘unarmed and disarming peace’ in assisi, 27.10.2026 red week an initiative launched by the pontifical foundation aid to the church in need (acn). week of witness 15 – 22 november. according to the latest figures provided by acn, 413 million christians live in countries where serious violations of religious freedom occur, and around 220 million christians worldwide are directly exposed to persecution. forms of persecution physical violence: torture, imprisonment, and murder are common, with open attacks on christians, often resulting in mass killings or displacements. property and church destruction: in countries like pakistan and egypt, churches are frequently attacked, vandalised, or demolished. often, believers face legal obstacles i n constructing new places of worship. legal restrictions: laws against ‘blasphemy, ’ ‘anti-conversion’ laws, or against ‘apostasy’ are used to intimidate and criminalise christians in countries like paki stan, saudi arabia, and iran. there have been more martyrdoms in the last hundred years than in the previ ous 1,900 years of church history. on wednesday 18th november we will offer mass for all those who suff er for the faith around the world. forty hours adoration for the solemnity of christ the king in the cathedral, mullingar from friday 20th to sunday 22nd november. the sacrament of reconciliation will be available from noon to midnight on saturday 21st. adoration will conclude with solemn vespers & benediction at 4pm on sunday led by bishop deenihan, with bishop fintan monahan as homilist. the cosy café will meet on tuesday 10th november in kilbeggan parish centre from 11am – 1pm. there will be tea/coffee and cakes and time for a chat with friends. the guest speaker this month is from age friendly ireland and they will provide information on the age friendly programme. music by joe kelly and johnny butterfield. those who have dementia, their family and carers are all welcome.
